info.description:
Disaster Alert API is a mission-control backend for disaster intelligence, community incident reports, SOS escalation, assistance coordination, emergency messaging, public alerts, chats, notifications, and administrator response operations.

================================
QUICK START
================================

Use this Swagger page to test the API safely.

For mobile/user endpoints:
1. Register or login using /auth/register or /auth/login.
2. Copy the token from the login response.
3. Click Authorize.
4. Paste it like this: Bearer YOUR_JWT_TOKEN.
5. Test endpoints such as /reports, /alerts, /sos, /assistance, /notifications, and /chats.

For admin endpoints:
1. Enter the Admin API Key under AdminApiKeyAuth.
2. Create or validate a privilege code.
3. Enter the full privilege code under PrivilegeCodeAuth.
4. Test admin endpoints such as /admin/reports, /admin/alerts, /admin/sos, /admin/assistance, and /admin/chats.

================================
AUTHENTICATION GUIDE
================================

1. Mobile/User endpoints use BearerAuth.
Required header:
Authorization: Bearer <JWT_TOKEN>

2. Basic admin management endpoints use AdminApiKeyAuth.
Required header:
Sigtrack-Admin-API-Key: <ADMIN_API_KEY>

3. Privileged admin operation endpoints require BOTH AdminApiKeyAuth and PrivilegeCodeAuth.
Required headers:
Sigtrack-Admin-API-Key: <ADMIN_API_KEY>
X-Privilege-Code: <GENERATED_UUID>

================================
ADMIN PRIVILEGE CODE FLOW
================================

Step 1: Click Authorize in Swagger.
Step 2: Enter your Admin API Key under AdminApiKeyAuth.
Step 3: Call POST /admin/privilege-codes to generate a privilege UUID.
Step 4: Copy the full UUID from data.code in the response.
Step 5: Click Authorize again and paste the UUID under PrivilegeCodeAuth.
Step 6: Test protected admin endpoints.

Important:
The full UUID is returned only once during creation.
codePrefix is only for display and audit logs. Do not use codePrefix as X-Privilege-Code.

================================
COMMON REQUEST NOTES
================================

POST and PUT endpoints usually require a request body.
Open the endpoint in Swagger and check the Parameters section.
For JSON endpoints, send Content-Type: application/json.
For upload endpoints, send Content-Type: multipart/form-data.

Required fields are marked as required in the request schema or form fields.
Optional fields can be omitted unless your frontend needs them.
Date/time fields should use ISO format where possible, for example: 2026-09-10T08:30:00Z.

================================
ADMIN PERMISSION CATALOG
================================

Reports:
- reports:read
- reports:approve

Assistance:
- assistance:read
- assistance:update_status

SOS:
- sos:read
- sos:update_status

Alerts:
- alerts:read
- alerts:create
- alerts:update
- alerts:delete

Chats:
- chats:read
- chats:send

Notifications:
- notifications:read
- notifications:send

Privilege Management:
- privilege_codes:create
- privilege_codes:read
- privilege_codes:revoke
- audit_logs:read
info.title: Disaster Alert API

post.description:
Creates a manual emergency alert from the admin dashboard.

Use this endpoint when an admin wants to publish a flood warning, fire outbreak, weather danger, health risk, security threat, or other public safety alert.
The alert can later be shown to users based on country/location and can also be delivered through notifications or WebSocket updates.

SECURITY:
This endpoint requires BOTH AdminApiKeyAuth and PrivilegeCodeAuth.

REQUIRED PERMISSION:
alerts:create

EXAMPLE REQUEST BODY:
{"title":"Heavy Rainfall Warning","description":"Heavy rainfall expected in flood-prone areas.","category":"weather","severity":"high","latitude":5.6037,"longitude":-0.1870,"country":"Ghana","region":"Greater Accra","address":"Accra"}

get.description:
Returns privilege-code records created for organisations, departments, units, or admin levels.

SECURITY:
This endpoint requires only AdminApiKeyAuth.

IMPORTANT:
The full UUID is not returned here for security reasons.
Only codePrefix is returned so admins can identify the record without exposing the full secret UUID.

Use this endpoint to review active, revoked, expired, and previously created privilege codes.

parameters.description: Maximum number of privilege-code records to return. Default is 50. Maximum is 200.
parameters.name: limit

401.description: Admin API key missing or invalid

post.description:
Creates a new privilege code for an organisation, unit, department, or admin level.

This endpoint is used to generate the UUID that will later be sent in the X-Privilege-Code header.
It requires only the Admin API Key because this endpoint is used to create privilege codes.

HOW TO USE IN SWAGGER:
1. Click Authorize.
2. Enter Sigtrack-Admin-API-Key under AdminApiKeyAuth.
3. Execute this endpoint.
4. Copy data.code from the response.
5. Click Authorize again.
6. Paste data.code under PrivilegeCodeAuth.

IMPORTANT:
The full UUID is returned only once during creation.
The codePrefix is only for display and audit logs. Do not use codePrefix as X-Privilege-Code.

EXAMPLE PERMISSIONS:
assistance:read, assistance:update_status, sos:read, sos:update_status, reports:read, reports:approve, alerts:read, alerts:create, alerts:update, alerts:delete

put.description:
Disables a privilege UUID so it can no longer be used on protected admin endpoints.

SECURITY:
This endpoint requires only AdminApiKeyAuth.

WHAT REVOKE MEANS:
Revoke does not delete the database record.
It changes the privilege-code status from active to revoked.
The old UUID stops working, but the record remains for audit history.

WHEN TO REVOKE:
Revoke a code when it is leaked, no longer trusted, assigned to the wrong level, or needs to be replaced by a new UUID.

400.description: Invalid request or privilege code already revoked

- When a privilege code was revoked
- Which admin endpoint was accessed
- Which permission was required
- Whether access was allowed or denied
- The codePrefix, organisation, level, IP address, and user agent involved

Returns incident reports.

When called from /admin/reports, this returns user-submitted reports for admin review.
Admin must provide both AdminApiKeyAuth and PrivilegeCodeAuth with `reports:read` permission.

If this handler is exposed on /reports, make sure normal users only see reports they are allowed to see.
Do not expose all users' reports to normal mobile users.

The admin should review the description, location, media evidence, reporter information, and status.

REQUIRED PERMISSION:

parameters.description: Report ID. This is the MongoDB ObjectID of the report.
parameters.name: id

put.description:
Approves a pending user-submitted report and converts it into a public alert.

WHAT HAPPENS WHEN THIS ENDPOINT IS CALLED:
1. Backend finds the report by ID.
2. Backend checks that the report is not already approved or rejected.
3. Backend creates a new public alert from the report.
4. Backend copies report media into alert imageUrls or videoUrls.
5. Backend updates the report status to approved.
6. Backend sends notifications and WebSocket updates where configured.

IMPORTANT:
Use this endpoint only after an admin has verified that the report is credible.
A normal mobile user should not be allowed to call this endpoint.

REQUIRED HEADERS:
- Sigtrack-Admin-API-Key: Your admin API key.
- X-Privilege-Code: A valid privilege code with `reports:approve`.

REQUIRED PERMISSION:
reports:approve
put.summary: Approve a report and publish it as a public alert

parameters.description: Report ID to approve. This must be a pending report ID.
parameters.name: id

200.description: Report approved and public alert created successfully. Response includes alertId and alert.

400.description: Report cannot be approved. It may already be approved, rejected, or invalid.

401.description: Missing or invalid Admin API Key.

403.description: Missing, revoked, expired, or unauthorized privilege code.

500.description: Failed to approve report because of server, repository, or database error.

get.description:
Establishes a real-time WebSocket connection for the admin dashboard.

Admin WebSocket URL:
wss://disaster-alert-backend-tiql.onrender.com/api/v1/admin/ws

Required header:
Sigtrack-Admin-API-Key: YOUR_ADMIN_API_KEY

Event format:
{"type":"EVENT_NAME","data":{}}

Admin dashboard events:
SOS_CREATED - sent when a user creates an SOS request.
ASSISTANCE_CREATED - sent when a user submits an assistance request.
REPORT_CREATED - sent when a user submits a report.
ALERT_CREATED - sent when an active alert is created.
ALERT_APPROVED - sent when an alert/report is approved.
CHAT_MESSAGE_CREATED - sent when a user sends a chat message.

SOS_CREATED example:
{"type":"SOS_CREATED","data":{"id":"sos_id","user":{"id":"user_id","name":"User","email":"user@email.com","phone":"0240000000","location":{"country":"Ghana","region":"Greater Accra","address":"Accra"}},"emergencyType":"medical","message":"Need help","latitude":5.6037,"longitude":-0.1870,"address":"Accra","status":"active","createdAt":"2026-06-11T10:00:00Z"}}

ASSISTANCE_CREATED example:
{"type":"ASSISTANCE_CREATED","data":{"id":"assistance_id","user":{"id":"user_id","name":"User","email":"user@email.com"},"assistanceType":"medical","urgencyLevel":"high","affectedIndividuals":3,"address":"Accra","status":"pending","createdAt":"2026-06-11T10:00:00Z"}}

post.description:
Allows an authenticated mobile user to report an emergency, disaster, hazard, or incident.

The report is saved as `pending` first.
It does not become a public alert until an admin reviews and approves it.

WHEN TO USE THIS ENDPOINT:
Use this when a mobile user wants to report flooding, fire, road accident, health outbreak, weather danger, security incident, or another emergency.

AUTH REQUIRED:
This endpoint requires a valid user JWT token.
Click Authorize and paste: Bearer YOUR_JWT_TOKEN

REQUEST OPTIONS:
This same endpoint supports two request types:

1. JSON request for reports without file upload.
Content-Type: application/json

Example JSON body:
{
"category": "flood",
"description": "Flooding has started around the roadside and vehicles cannot pass.",
"timeOfOccurrence": "2026-09-10T08:30:00Z",
"latitude": 5.6037,
"longitude": -0.1870,
"address": "Circle, Accra",
"country": "Ghana",
"region": "Greater Accra"
}

2. Multipart request for reports with image or video upload.
Content-Type: multipart/form-data
Use the form field named `media` for the uploaded file.

REQUIRED FIELDS:
- category: Type of incident. Example: flood
- description: What happened. Example: Flooding has blocked the road.
- timeOfOccurrence: When it happened. Example: 2026-09-10T08:30:00Z
- latitude: Incident latitude. Example: 5.6037
- longitude: Incident longitude. Example: -0.1870

OPTIONAL FIELDS:
- address: Human-readable location or landmark.
- country: Country name.
- region: Region/state name.
- media: Optional image or video file.
